properties.headline: Flood Warning issued October 13 at 10:11AM EDT by NWS Melbourne FL
properties.description:
...The Flood Warning continues for the following rivers in Florida...

St Johns River Near Astor affecting Lake and Volusia Counties.

.The St Johns River at Astor has fallen into Minor Flood Stage, as
upstream heavy rainfall continues to drain through the basin. River
levels are forecast to fall through Minor Flood Stage this week.

For the St. Johns River...including Astor...Minor flooding is
forecast.

* WHAT...Minor flooding is occurring and minor flooding is forecast.

* WHERE...St Johns River near Astor.

* WHEN...Until further notice.

* IMPACTS...At 3.0 feet, Water approaches or may enter lowest homes
on or near Wildhog Road and nearby canals. Flooding reaches the
parking lot of the Juno Trail Apartments. Flooding on portions of
Alligator Road and Holiday Road. Lowest lying yards along Blue
Creek are flooded. Roads at Astor Landing Campground and Lake
Dexter Boat Ramp begin to flood. Water enters lower homes closest
to the river on McPherson Lane.

* ADDITIONAL DETAILS...
- At 9:30 AM EDT Tuesday the stage was 2.9 feet.
- Bankfull stage is 2.0 feet.
- Recent Activity...The maximum river stage in the 24 hours ending
at 9:30 AM EDT Tuesday was 3.1 feet.
- Forecast...The river is expected to remain steady above flood
stage at 2.9 feet.
- Flood stage is 2.3 feet.
- http://www.weather.gov/safety/flood
properties.instruction:
Motorists should not attempt to drive around barricades or drive cars
through flooded areas.

Caution is urged when walking near riverbanks.

Additional information is available at www.weather.gov.

The next statement will be issued this evening at 1100 PM EDT.

properties.headline: Hydrologic Outlook issued October 13 at 5:31PM ChST by NWS Tiyan GU
properties.description:
ESFGUM

This Hydrologic Outlook is for Guam, Rota, Tinian, and Saipan.

Invest 96W is still a broad, disorganized disturbance located about
300 miles north of Kosrae. Ensemble model guidance continues to show
a passage anywhere between south of Guam to north of Saipan as a
tropical storm or typhoon. Uncertainty is still high regarding
timing, location, and intensity, but the potential for locally heavy
rainfall and flooding continues to increase approaching this weekend.

This is expected to produce 5 to 8 inches of rainfall between
Saturday and Monday, with localized amounts up to 12 inches possible.

As showers are likely to persist, consistent rainfall is likely to
saturate the soils enough to increase chance for mudslides.

Residents on these islands need to closely monitor this developing
situation as flood watches, advisories and flash flood warnings could
be issued later this weekend.

If living near streams and rivers, prepare to move items away from
stream and river banks. Make sure storm drains nearby are not
clogged, especially If living at low-lying areas.

properties.headline: Special Weather Statement issued October 13 at 1:49PM ChST by NWS Tiyan GU
properties.description:
Invest 96W is currently rated as "Medium" by the Joint Typhoon
Warning Center, meaning tropical cyclone development is likely, but
beyond 24 hours. It's currently located west of Ujae near 9.3N
164.4E. It continues to slowly organize and strengthen north of
Kosrae/east-northest of Pohnpei.

Inflow into the developing disturbance will allow for locally heavy
rainfall to develop, with over 1 inch per hour rain rates probable
from time to time. Rainfall totals will likely be 2 to 5 inches
tonight through Thursday, with locally higher amounts possible.
Winds will also increase as 96W strengthens, and at least isolated
wind gusts to 30 knots are possible with any heavy shower or
thunderstorm that develops.

Gusty winds and elevated, choppy seas will make marine conditions
difficult. Residents may need to reconsider plans for inter-island
boating as the week continues. Also keep up to date with the latest
information from your local emergency management agency.

properties.headline: Hydrologic Outlook issued October 12 at 10:07AM AKDT by NWS Juneau AK
properties.description:
ESFAJK

An atmospheric river will move into the region Thursday, driving
heavy rain across much of the Panhandle into the weekend. However,
areas south of Frederick Sound will likely see the heaviest rain.
Anticipate 24 hour rainfall amounts to reach 3 to 5 inches at sea
level for many communities south of Frederick Sound, with localized
areas near Ketchikan and Misty Fjords closer to 4 to 6 inches,
especially in the mountains. At this time, the primary threat is many
rivers and streams reaching bankfull conditions with ponding of water
on roads and areas of poor drainage. Mariners, check those bilge
pumps.

Significant rises and flooding in rivers is possible but at this time
there exists large variability in how rain develops and persists
across the southern Panhandle.

Stay tuned to weather.gov/juneau as we continue to assess the
situation and make updates to the forecast.

properties.headline: Air Quality Alert issued October 12 at 10:39AM EDT by NWS Marquette MI
properties.description:
The Michigan Department of Environmental Quality has issued an Air
Quality Alert for Monday October 12, for elevated levels of
fine particulates (PM2.5) due to wildfire smoke. Localized pollutants
levels within those area may reach the Unhealthy for Sensitive
Groups with the the potential for Unhealthy.

The alert is in effect for the following Michigan Counties,

Menominee, Dickinson, Iron, Marquette, and Baraga.

It is recommended that, when possible, you avoid strenuous outdoor
activities, especially those with heart disease and respiratory
diseases such as asthma.

Monitor for symptoms such as wheezing, coughing, chest tightness,
dizziness, or burning in nose, throat, and eyes. Reduce or eliminate
activities that contribute to air pollution, such as outdoor
burning, and use of residential wood burning devices.

Keep windows closed overnight to prevent smoke from getting indoors
and, if possible, run central air conditioning with MERV-13 or
higher rated filters.

For further information, please see EPA's Air Now site for up-to-
date air quality data at https://www.airnow.gov

For further health information, please see MDHHS' Wildfire Smoke and
Your Health site at https://www.michigan.gov/mdhhs/safety-injury-
prev/environmental-health/your-health-and-wildfire-smoke.
